# Spec-owned paths — the list behind the "spec change" label gate.
#
# Read by .github/scripts/check-spec-label.sh on every PR (workflow:
# .github/workflows/spec-label.yml). A PR whose diff touches ANY path
# matching a pattern here must carry the "spec change" label; it fails
# CI otherwise. These are the files where behaviour, wording and the
# rules for agents live — the things AGENTS.md says decide what the app
# does and how it looks.
#
# Format: one pattern per line. Blank lines and lines starting with '#'
# are skipped. Matching is bash [[ $file == $pattern ]] glob semantics:
# '*' crosses '/', so 'design/*' also matches 'design/screens/x.md'.
# Pattern order doesn't matter; keep it grouped for readability.
#
# Not every match also needs a changelog entry — that second gate is a
# shorter list inside the script (needs_spec_log / needs_design_log).

# --- Behaviour spec and its map ---
docs/SPEC.md
docs/README.md
docs/DEVIN_KICKOFF.md
docs/analysis/*

# --- Agent rules ---
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md

# --- Behaviour-bearing config and prompts ---
# Prompts are immutable once used (AGENTS.md rule 8); config.example.yaml
# holds every spec threshold; .env.example defines the env contract.
backend/prompts/*.md
backend/config.example.yaml
.env.example

# --- Look and wording ---
design/*

# --- The gate itself ---
# A change to the check, its pattern list or its workflow is a process
# change — it needs the label like any other spec edit.
.github/spec-paths.txt
.github/scripts/check-spec-label.sh
.github/workflows/spec-label.yml
